reason: I rank loop_order first because it tests B reuse through traversal with no packing cost and preserves each tile’s reduction order. Cache conflict padding is a small, distinct layout probe, though the supplied evidence does not show a conflict. The B packing proposals test contiguous access but add packing and allocation inside gemm; cache_blocking, panel_packing, and b_panel_layout overlap heavily, so I would test one representative first. A transpose packing and the combined two-operand packing add more work and have uncertain locality payoff; scratch_lifetime and transpose_fusion also alter traversal or repeat data movement. The fresh baseline varies widely (878–1390 GFLOP/s), and the paired-load-only experiment regressed in every fresh pair, so none of this supports a performance claim. I rank the independent MOPA schedule and full-tile store simplification ahead of output-transfer variants because their changes are narrower; the supplied probes and tutorial are not hill measurements. Repeated store-path proposals are ranked later because they substantially duplicate one another.
